born 30 January 1982) is a Senegalese former professional [[basketball]] player who is head coach for the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the [[NBA G League]], as well as the [[Senegal men's national basketball team|Senegal national team]]. ==Early life== Diop played soccer while growing up in Senegal. He began practicing basketball at the age of 15 and moved to the U.S. to play for Oak Hill Academy, where he succeeded in averaging 14.6 points, 13.2 rebounds, and 8.1 blocks during his senior year.[https://assets.espn.go.com/highschool/a/000426diop.html Diop declares for NBA draft] He earned the [[USA Today]] [[Virginia]] Player of the Year title and led [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]], to a #1 nation ranking (33 wins, 0 losses).{{cite magazine |last=Fussman |first=Cal |date= July 9, 2002|title=Next Voices: DeSagana Diop |url= https://www.espn.com/magazine/vol4no14diop.html |magazine=[[ESPN The Magazine]] |location= |publisher= [[ESPN]]|access-date=March 18, 2024}} Diop speaks five languages:[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/community/rta_diop_050302.html Cavaliers: Cavalier DeSagana Diop Holds a Special Reading Timeout in French with St. Ignatius High School Students] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080312004956/http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/community/rta_diop_050302.html |date=2008-03-12 }} [[Arabic]], [[English language|English]], [[French language|French]], [[Wolof language|Wolof]] and some [[Spanish language|Spanish]]. ==Professional career== === Cleveland Cavaliers (2001–2005) === Diop was drafted directly out of Oak Hill Academy by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] with the 8th overall pick of the [[2001 NBA draft]].{{cite news| url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/nba/01draft/draft-board.htm | work=USA Today | title=2001 NBA draft board | date=July 2, 2001 | access-date=May 1, 2010}} He was the fifth high school player, after [[Kwame Brown]], [[Tyson Chandler]], [[Eddy Curry]] and [[Ousmane Cisse]] to declare for the draft. As a reserve center, he played 193 games in four seasons with the Cavaliers, averaging 1.6 points, 2.6 [[rebound (sports)|rebounds]] and 0.8 [[block (basketball)|blocks]] in 10.8 minutes per contest. On November 23, 2002, Diop dropped a career-high 10 points in a 97–84 loss to the [[New Orleans Hornets]]. The Cavaliers struggled heavily in Diop's first few years with the team. The franchise eventually began to improve with the addition of an 18-year-old [[LeBron James]] in the [[2003 NBA draft]]. In the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]], the Cavaliers had posted their best record since the [[1997–98 NBA season|1997–98 season]], going 42–40. However, they still missed the playoffs and this was Diop's final year with the team. === Dallas Mavericks (2005–2008) === Diop signed a three-year contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] as a [[free agent]] on August 19, 2005.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/mavericks/news/mavs_sign_diop_081905.html |title=Mavs Sign Diop |work=[[NBA.com]] | date=2009-08-19 | access-date=2009-02-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070822132807/http://www.nba.com/mavericks/news/mavs_sign_diop_081905.html|archive-date=August 22, 2007}} Diop, a defensive player who specialized in shot blocking and rebounding, shared the center position with [[Erick Dampier]]. He had joined a winning team, and the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]] was Diop's most successful season regarding playoff success as the Mavericks went 60–22, made a deep playoff push and reached the [[2006 NBA Finals|2006 Finals]]. The Mavericks ended up losing the finals in six games to the [[Miami Heat]]. Against the [[New York Knicks]] in a pre-season game, Diop hit the game-winning tip-in off of a missed shot by [[Keith Van Horn]]. On November 15, 2005, Diop recorded a career-high 16 rebounds in an 83–80 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]]. In that same game, Diop also recorded a career-high 6 blocks—including a denial of [[Carmelo Anthony]]'s potentially game-winning field goal attempt.[https://web.archive.org/web/20210225023116/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=251115006 ESPN – Denver vs. Dallas Recap, November 15, 2005] On January 14, 2006, he became a full-time starter for the Mavericks for the rest of the regular season and into the playoffs, assisting in the Mavericks qualifying for the [[2006 NBA Finals]] as representatives of the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/diopde01/gamelog/2006/|title=DeSagana Diop 2005-06 Game Log|website=[[Basketball Reference]]|access-date=14 April 2020}} In March 2006, two Mavericks fans produced a version of the [[hip hop]] song "[[Jump (Kris Kross song)|Jump]]" by [[Kris Kross]]. In their version, the refrain "Jump! Jump!" was turned into "Diop! Diop!", and the video praises Diop's shotblocking ability. It became so popular that the Mavs started to play the video at their home games. Diop said, "I remember the first time they played the video during a timeout and I was trying to pay attention to what coach [Johnson] was trying to say but I was sneaking looks at the video."[http://www.yaysports.com/nba/2006/03/the_miggidymiggidy_mavs_will_m.html] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060513201920/http://www.yaysports.com/nba/2006/03/the_miggidymiggidy_mavs_will_m.html|date=May 13, 2006}} For the 2005–06 season, he ranked 11th in total blocks, 14th in blocks per game, and 4th in blocks per 48 minutes.[https://www.espn.com/nba/stats/player/_/season/2006/seasontype/2/table/defensive/sort/avgBlocks/dir/desc ESPN – NBA Statistics and League Leaders – National Basketball Association] In Game 7 of the 2006 Western Conference Semifinals between San Antonio and Dallas, Diop, playing with a broken nose, grabbed three offensive rebounds (four total), and blocked two of [[Tim Duncan]]'s shots in the second and fourth quarters and overtime.[https://web.archive.org/web/20161025173627/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260522024 Mavs blow 20-point lead before eliminating Spurs in OT] On April 11, 2007, Diop recorded his first double-double with season highs of 10 points and 15 rebounds in the Mavs' franchise-high 30th road victory, a 105–88 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20161025112348/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270411016 Mavericks set franchise record with 30th road victory] The Mavericks finished the [[2006–07 Dallas Mavericks season|2006–07 season]] even more successful than the previous season, with a franchise best 67–15 record. They were extremely dominant throughout the season, and unlike the previous season, they were expected to reach the finals again.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}} They grabbed the first seed in the Western Conference, and matched up with the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the first round. The Warriors had gone 42–40 and were barely a winning team that season, they were expected to be heavily outmatched by the Mavericks. However, the Warriors won the series in 6 games, making the Mavericks only the third top seed in NBA history to lose in the first round. === New Jersey Nets (2008) === On February 19, 2008, Diop was traded to the [[New Jersey Nets]], along with signed-and-traded [[Keith Van Horn]], [[Devin Harris]], [[Trenton Hassell]], [[Maurice Ager]], and roughly $3 million cash and [[2008 NBA draft|2008]] and [[2010 NBA draft|2010]] first-round draft picks in exchange for [[Jason Kidd]], [[Malik Allen]], and [[Antoine Wright (basketball)|Antoine Wright]].{{cite web |last=Finley |first=Bill |date=February 20, 2008 |title=Kidd Really Is Traded to Dallas This Time |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/02/20/sports/basketball/20nets.html |access-date=May 23, 2023 |website=The New York Times}} Diop never achieved the same team success as he did in the 2005–06 and 2006–07 seasons as the Nets entered a stage of rebuilding and finished the [[2007–08 New Jersey Nets season|2007–08 season]] with a mediocre 34–48 record and missed the playoffs. === Return to Dallas (2008–2009) === On July 9, 2008, Diop signed a six-year, $32 million contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/mavericks/news/Diop_and_Barea_sign070908.html |title=Diop back in the fold |work=[[NBA.com]] | date=2008-07-09 |access-date=2009-02-28}} Diop's return to Dallas was short as he didn't finish the [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09 season]] with the team. === Charlotte Bobcats (2009–2013) === On January 16, 2009, Diop was traded to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] for guard [[Matt Carroll (basketball)|Matt Carroll]] and center [[Ryan Hollins]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_diop_090116.html |title=Bobcats Acquire DeSagana Diop from Dallas Mavericks |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2009-01-16 |access-date=2009-01-16 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090120011642/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_diop_090116.html |archive-date=2009-01-20 }} Diop spent the rest of his playing career with the Charlotte Bobcats. The Bobcats had been a struggling team for the past few years prior but they had been steadily improving and finished the [[2008–09 Charlotte Bobcats season|2008–09 season]] 35–47 and missed the playoffs by four wins. In the following [[2009–10 NBA season|2009–10 season]], the Bobcats, led by All-Star [[Gerald Wallace]] and leader [[Stephen Jackson]], went 44–38 and made the playoffs as the 7th seed in the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]]. They lost to the [[Orlando Magic]] in a four-game sweep. Diop continued to play for the team; however, the roster had drastically changed in the following seasons and he missed the playoffs for the rest of his career. In the following season the Bobcats only went 34–48 and the team's roster had shifted as Charlotte entered another rebuild. In the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]] the Bobcats made history by having the worst record in NBA history, ending the season with a 7–59 record. In an especially embarrassing moment, Diop missed a free throw attempt that fell several feet short of the baseline in a January 28 102-99 loss to the [[2011-12 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]].January 28th 102-99 loss to the [[2011-12 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]] Diop only played one more season with the Bobcats and they missed the playoffs in the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13 season]]. On March 4, 2013, Diop played his final NBA game; a 105–122 loss hosted by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], in which he recorded two points, two rebounds, one block and a foul in over 15 minutes of playing time.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/diopde01/gamelog/2013|title=DeSagana Diop 2012-13 Game Log|website=[[Basketball Reference]]|publisher=[[Sports Reference]]|date=2013|accessdate=1 June 2022}} On September 30, 2013, Diop signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/training-camp-roster-130930 Cavaliers Announce 2013-14 Training Camp Roster] However, he was waived on October 25 before the season started.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14637 |title=Cavs waive DeSagana Diop, Kenny Kadji, Jermaine Taylor, Elliot Williams |access-date=2013-10-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029195753/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14637 |archive-date=2013-10-29 |url-status=dead }} Diop retired from the NBA shortly after{{When|date=June 2020}} at 31 years old. ==Coaching career== On November 11, 2014, Diop joined the coaching staff of the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as a player development coach.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/dfw/news/nick-van-exel-desagana-diop-join-legends-coaching-staff/|title=Nick Van Exel, DeSagana Diop Join Legends' Coaching Staff|work=CBSLocal.com|date=November 11, 2014|access-date=November 11, 2014}} On October 19, 2015, he was promoted to assistant coach.{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5061270|title=Legends Round out Coaches' Bench|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 19, 2015|access-date=October 19, 2015}} On October 3, 2016, Diop was hired by the [[Utah Jazz]] as a coaching associate.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-announce-basketball-staff-addition|title=Jazz Announce Basketball Staff Addition|work=NBA.com|date=October 3, 2016|access-date=October 3, 2016}} On November 30, 2020, Diop was hired by the [[Houston Rockets]] as an assistant coach.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-announce-additions-coaching-staff|title=Rockets Announce Additions to Coaching Staff|work=NBA.com|date=November 30, 2020|access-date=November 30, 2020}} Prior to the 2022-23 season, Diop left the Rockets organization and was appointed head coach of the [[Westchester Knicks]], the [[New York Knicks]]' G League affiliate.{{cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2022/05/26/knicks-hire-desagana-diop-as-new-nba-g-league-coach/|title=Knicks' new G League coach DeSagana Diop comes with Jazz intrigue|work=New York Post|date=May 26, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2022}} On August 12, 2025, it was announced that Diop was the head coach for the [[Senegal men's national basketball team]] in the upcoming [[FIBA AfroBasket]] tournament.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/nets/news/former-net-to-lead-home-country-in-international-competition|title=Former Net to Lead Home Country in International
